The release's first seed boot died and was retried on every run: the seed booted the whole tree under eval; it now runs through Barkpark.Release.seed() without admission and a first boot goes straight to ready. One slow request no longer restarts the runtime: recovery needs three missed probes in a row. The release rehearsal passes its four checks on the fixed boot. 2026-10-01 afternoon: the disk image. build-mac-app.mjs --dmg writes release/Barkdown-0.6.0-arm64.dmg, 165 MB; the rehearsal mounts it read-only, copies the application out as a person drags it, detaches, and the packaged rehearsal (first boot, note, restart; no agent package inside; under 650 MB) passes against that installed copy. Ad hoc signed, not notarized: another Mac's Gatekeeper refuses it until the signature exists. Later the same afternoon: a SHA-256 is written beside the image and verified by the rehearsal; removing the installed application leaves the user data where it was, and the application reinstalled from the image opens the same library and reads the same note (A5: artifact integrity, uninstall preserves user data). Six checks. A5 daily-use checks on the carried runtime (9 findings): keyboard-only reaches New page, the work pane, the composer and Send, and Settings opens with the shortcut; the focused composer is indicated by its frame; no sideways scroll at 200% zoom or in an 820 px window; reduced motion now collapses every animation; a 400-paragraph note writes in 260 ms, opens in 102 ms and saves a typed line in 481 ms. Observed, not fixed: at 200% zoom the 1300 px window is 650 CSS px wide, the layout is the narrow one and New page sits behind the collapsed sidebar. The failed-upgrade case: a replacement bundle without its runtime does not start the library and leaves the profile data untouched — it now says "This copy of Barkdown is missing the runtime it should carry. Reinstall Barkdown from its disk image; your notes and profiles are kept." — and the previous bundle put back opens the same library (A5: failed-upgrade rollback preserves profiles).
